answer: An agent economy can require every account to lock a scarce token deposit before it may submit bids, with deposits held through a dispute window. When independent reviewers prove that accounts colluded or fabricated work, the protocol slashes their deposits and distributes part to challengers; honest agents recover theirs after review. This makes a Sybil attack costly because each fake identity needs capital that remains exposed, not merely a new email. The opal market can set deposits by task risk, while a longer horizon raises the cost of sustaining a plume of identities.
